purpose: Separate conditional tolerance assessment; never recalibration of baseline survival probabilities

FAO.method: Mean rootzone saturated-paste ECe; fairly uniform salinity from late seedling to maturity; predominantly chloride salts
FAO.limitation: Different experiments, not standardized head-to-head trial; sulfate-rich and perchlorate mixtures not validated
FAO.license: Not verified; paraphrase facts with attribution

RYE1989.method: Two-year field plots; Holtville silty clay; irrigation salinized with NaCl/CaCl2 1:1 mass; saturation-extract EC
RYE1989.limitation: Emergence more sensitive than later growth; grain and straw endpoints differ

CRESS2010.method: Four replicates of 5kg loamy soil pots; initial pH7.6 and8.75% CaCO3; NaCl applied to established seedlings; maturity biomass and survival
CRESS2010.EC_extraction: Unspecified; EC meter reported, not verified ECe
CRESS2010.limitation: No transferable threshold/slope; starting pH observation not pH dose-response

TOMATO_PH2007.method: T3238 and iron-inefficient mutant; hydroponic pH5.0 versus7.5; Fe and nitrogen forms manipulated
TOMATO_PH2007.finding: Wildtype lacked chlorosis at pH 7.5 with Fe-EDTA but became chlorotic without iron. Absence of chlorosis does not imply unchanged biomass or harmless alkalinity; no universal soil-pH exclusion threshold.

TOMATO_CLO4_2005.finding: Tomato fruit accumulated less than leaves; contaminated-water garden samples contained perchlorate
TOMATO_CLO4_2005.limitation: Not a growth threshold, food-safety certificate, or Phoenix dose response

crops.cultivar_warning: Baseline cultivar not verified; cherry tomato separately1.7/9.1 in FAO

crops.endpoint: NaCl survival/biomass evidence; no compatible ECe curve

EC.instruction: Phoenix WCL dilute extract EC is not saturated-paste ECe, irrigation-water EC or rhizosphere exposure; never insert it into these crop curves

pH.instruction: Phoenix extraction pH can flag alkaline nutrient-availability concerns, not establish a plantability cutoff; extraction method and treatment differ

Ca_Mg_K.instruction: Presence does not establish adequate nutrition, balance, bioavailability or absence of toxicity; no crop-ranking bonus

Na_Cl.instruction: Salinity relevance, but no Phoenix-mixture crop-specific dose-response verified; do not equate NaCl tests with full Phoenix mixture

SO4.instruction: Chloride-dominant ECe guidelines cannot be assumed valid for sulfate-rich mixtures; retain chemistry flag rather than automatic penalty

ClO4.instruction: Retain unresolved growth and edible-tissue safety flag for every crop; tomato accumulation evidence means growth is not food safety

NH4.instruction: Preserve original detection/interference qualifier; no confirmed fertility credit or N-sufficiency inference

independent_scenario.implemented_output: Source-qualified threshold-exceedance flags only; no relative yield calculation

conclusion: For independent prepared-substrate ECe scenarios under chloride-dominant source conditions, grain-rye has a higher reported yield threshold than generic tomato fruit and carrot storage-root. This can motivate salinity-specific experiments, not rank absolute productivity or actual Phoenix viability. Cress remains quantitatively unresolved. The original model results are preserved, not newly validated under Phoenix chemistry.
